answer: The Sybil defence I trust most bonds each identity to a proof-of-personhood root, so cost is inherited by every downstream key. A new agent deposits reserve collateral slashed when two identities share a graph root. Since each extra claim on one human widens that penalty, cloning one person a thousand times costs the bond a thousand times. Cheap farms still echo into the ledger, but as expense rather than leverage: the marginal clone costs more than the yield it captures. That keeps ocean-sized participation narrow and honest, so cloned pigment cannot wash-trade.
